ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 and its Regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 23; Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), including the individuals with significant control (ISC) register for private corporations; and, for federal extra-provincial shareholders, Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s 21.1. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, ISC/UBOs, and corporate shareholders against: (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (iii) OFAC SDN list for any USD-denominated transactions; and (iv) domestic PEP and adverse-media databases. Enhanced due diligence, including independent source-of-wealth verification, applies to all foreign PEPs and to any cash deposit or wire transfer exceeding CAD 10,000, with FINTRAC large-cash and electronic-funds-transfer reporting as applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (ACRS - Alberta Corporate Registration System) administered by Service Alberta; name clearance is evidenced by a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report submitted with the Articles of Incorporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names under the ABCA must be formed of English and/or French words in Roman script; foreign-script names require a certified English/French transliteration accepted by the Registrar. Names must include a distinctive element, a permissible descriptive element, and a legal element (e.g., 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.'). Purely numeric names are reserved for numbered companies; formatting, abbreviations, and punctuation must follow NUANS conventions.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Trust Company, Loan, Loan Company, Insurance, Financial - require prior federal or provincial financial-services regulatory approval
University, College, Institute, Academy - require proof of authorization or ministerial consent
Royal, Crown, Government, Municipal, Police, Commission - prohibited absent governmental authorization
Co-operative and Society - reserved for entities incorporated under cooperative or societies statutes
Canada, Alberta, Calgary, Edmonton or other geographic terms - require evidence of place of business or consent
Amalgamated - permissible only in genuine amalgamation cases
Certified, Chartered, Accredited, Expert - require professional or credentialing evidence
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of rejection, obtain a fresh NUANS report and file a written reconsideration request with legal arguments to the Director of Corporate Registry, Service Alberta; where rejection is based on confusing similarity, attach a notarized consent letter from the existing name holder. If reconsideration is refused, challenge the decision by judicial review or statutory appeal to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the ABCA and Alberta Rules of Court (AR 124/2010) within 60 days of final refusal. As an interim option, incorporate a numbered company and apply for a name change once the desired name is cleared.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or agent-supplied registered office and records address is acceptable for corporate registry purposes; however, for ISIC 5630 beverage service the operational business requires a physical licensed premises satisfying Alberta Health Services (AHS) food-safety permits, municipal fire and occupancy approvals, and municipal business licensing. Virtual offices cannot satisfy operational premises requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - approximately 85% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation, driven by mandatory AHS food facility inspections, municipal licence compliance visits, and potential fire marshal occupancy checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA) — ss. 6 (incorporation), 9 (articles), 10 (directors), 101 (registered office)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (CorpReg Online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued upon filing Articles of Incorporation (Form 1), Notice of Registered Office (Form 2), and Notice of Directors (Form 3)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the ABCA; shares must not be issued for consideration less than fair value; no statutory escrow account is mandated for a fresh corporation's share subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription for common shares set out in the Articles of Incorporation be and is hereby accepted, and the stated capital be recorded as fully paid from the funds received from the subscribers; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be fixed at [Suite, Street, City, Alberta] and that [Agent name] act as registered agent; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons be appointed officers of the corporation: [President], [Secretary-Treasurer], and [Chief Financial Officer], each to serve until the next annual meeting; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers be and are hereby authorized and directed to execute and deliver all documents required to perfect incorporation, banking arrangements, and the licensed operation of the specialty tea salon.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (CorpReg Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search and reserve the proposed corporate name 'Specialty Tea Salon Lounge' or a numbered name; submit the reservation with the Articles of Incorporation. A name reservation is valid for 90 days and must be attached to the filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity, submit up to three alternative names within the reservation window or switch to a numbered corporation name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and File Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (CorpReg Online or authorized service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation), Form 2 (Notice of Registered Office), and Form 3 (Notice of Directors) electronically, pay the registration fee, and confirm at least one director who meets the ABCA residency requirements.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director from each proposed director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction inquiry, file an amended notice within 30 days; missing director consents may be submitted as a late cure to avoid rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the Articles and notices, the registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation and assigns the Alberta corporate number; request a certified copy for banking, leasing, and licensing purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed, use the registry's expedited certified copy service or obtain a Registry Status Certificate for immediate third-party proof.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for CRA Business Number and Tax Program Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a Business Number (BN) and program accounts: GST/HST (mandatory once annual gross revenue exceeds CAD 30,000), corporate income tax, and payroll (if employees are hired). Use Form RC1A or the Business Registration Online service.
required_dossiers: Completed RC1A form or CRA online registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries officer or address information, correct the RC1A and attach director identification or a lease agreement within the response window; the BN is typically issued within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Execute Organizational Minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered bank or credit union in Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate operating bank account per the First Board Resolution, deposit the stated capital, issue share certificates, and sign the organizational minutes and register of directors and registered office.
required_dossiers: Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's due diligence requires proof of business premises, provide a certified corporate extract and the executed lease for the tea salon lounge.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Health Services (Public Health Inspection) and the municipal business licensing authority for the city where the salon operates (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Business Licensing)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Service Establishment Permit (Alberta Public Health Act, Food Regulation, Alta Reg 202/2006) and Municipal Business Licence

environmental_impact_assessment.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment; classified as a low-risk food and beverage service operation requiring municipal sewer connection approval and, if any stormwater or grease interceptor modification is proposed, a self-registration report to AEPA.
environmental_impact_assessment.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Trade wastewater must connect to the municipal sanitary sewer and comply with the applicable city sewer bylaw (e.g., grease concentration not exceeding 100 mg/L and pH between 6.0 and 10.0); kitchen hood exhaust must meet Alberta Fire Code and municipal nuisance-free air emission standards; solid waste and used cooking oil must be removed by a licensed waste carrier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code (2023 Alberta Edition), municipal building occupancy and structural load clearance for seating/retail ceramic displays, and workplace safety clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Act, Regulation and Code, including a documented hazard assessment, fire suppression system, and staff training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — GST/HST and federal income tax administration; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA for the Province of Alberta under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act and the Canada–Alberta Tax Collection Agreement. Primary portal: CRA 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services/business-account.html); registration via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO); GST/HST filing via GST/HST NETFILE or EDI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate federally via Corporations Canada (or provincially via Alberta Corporate Registry 'CORES' under the Alberta Business Corporations Act) — an incorporation number is issued; no minimum capital is required for Alberta ABCA corporations and 100% non-resident ownership is permissible. 2) The CRA automatically creates a 9-digit Business Number (BN) for the corporation upon corporate registry data exchange; the BN acts as the master tax identifier. 3) Through BRO or Form RC1, open the required CRA program accounts: RC (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), and RP (payroll) — providing registered office address, director details, fiscal year-end, and estimated annual worldwide taxable revenue. 4) GST/HST registration is mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies (excluding certain zero-rated exports) exceed C$30,000 on a rolling four-consecutive-calendar-quarter basis (or a single calendar quarter for seasonal businesses); registration may be elected voluntarily before the threshold is met. 5) The corporation files a T2 corporate income tax return (which also computes Alberta tax under the collection agreement), and, if registrant, GST/HST returns (generally monthly/quarterly depending on revenue).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style 'check-the-box' election; a Canadian Business Corporation is statutorily a resident corporation taxable on worldwide income under Part I of the Income Tax Act. Alberta general corporate rate 8.0%; CCPC small business rate 2.0% on the first C$500,000 of active business income (Alberta). Relevant elections: (1) voluntary GST/HST registration under ETA s. 221(1) even while below the small-supplier threshold; (2) closely-related corporation nil-consideration election under ETA s. 156 (Form GST25) to disregard inter-corporate supplies for GST/HST; (3) corporate rollover elections on tax-deferred transfers to a corporation under ITA s. 85; (4) associated-corporation elections/allocations under ITA s. 256; (5) hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.2–18.8) are self-executing with no elective override.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) — Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST; Alberta has no provincial sales tax or HST component, so the combined rate in CA-AB is 5%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 — small-supplier threshold measured on total worldwide consideration for taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated exports), aggregated with associated persons, over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (or a single calendar quarter for seasonal operations); exceeding the threshold or anticipating its excess triggers mandatory GST registration with effect on the day small-supplier status ceases.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, digital stamping, or government pre-clearance API exists for Canadian GST/HST invoices. Requirements: (1) registrants must issue sales invoices containing prescribed information (vendor BN, date, description, tax amount, rate); (2) electronic filing of GST/HST returns is mandatory for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding C$1.5 million (GST/HST NETFILE), and T2 corporate returns must be e-filed for corporations with gross revenue over C$1 million; (3) CRA business APIs (e.g., BRO, GST/HST NETFILE, My Business Account) are available but optional; (4) payment and remittance must be made electronically when remittances exceed prescribed CRA thresholds.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under ETA Schedule VI: (a) Goods — s. 20 zero-rates tangible personal property supplied by the registrant and delivered to a destination outside Canada (e.g., packaged loose-leaf tea sold online to a foreign customer and shipped abroad); proof of export must be retained by the vendor. (b) Services — s. 7 zero-rates a supply of a service made to a non-resident who is not in Canada, unless the service is performed in respect of real property in Canada, tangible personal property in Canada, personal services rendered while the individual is in Canada, or intangible personal property used in Canada. In-salon food and beverage service consumed at the Alberta premises is standard-rated at 5% GST and is not zero-rated. A packaged-goods export accompanies zero-rating; the supplier may also recover input tax credits attributable to the zero-rated supply via the GST/HST General Rebate/Refund system, subject to CRA audit substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — filed electronically via the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS), including exporter BN, description of goods, value (CAD), weight, and destination (required unless exempt under the Export Reporting Regulations)
Commercial Invoice (Canada Customs Invoice equivalent) evidencing the sale and identifying the foreign buyer and destination

Shipping documentation — Original Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) or Canada Post/USPS or courier waybill showing the goods departed Canada; for services, the written contract, statement of work, and invoice to the non-resident counterparty

FX receipt evidence — bank statement / SWIFT MT103 confirmation of payment received from the non-resident (Canada does not issue a formal Inward Remittance Certificate; such banking evidence is used as the analogous documentary proof)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA has a four-year statutory reassessment window (ETA s. 298) for GST/HST assessments and refund reviews, but no limitation period applies where a return or claim contains a misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default, or fraud. Zero-rating may be retroactively clawed back if the prescribed export documentation is not maintained; the taxpayer bears the burden of proof and may lose input tax credits associated with the failed zero-rating. Penalties: failure to register under ETA s. 280 — the greater of C$250 and 5% of net tax; false statements or omissions under ETA s. 285(1) — the greater of C$250 and 25% of the net tax sought to be evaded; failure to file information returns — C$100 plus C$25/day. Criminal evasion under ETA s. 327.1: summary conviction fine up to 50% of evaded tax and up to 2 years less 1 day imprisonment; indictment fine up to 200% of evaded tax and up to 5 years imprisonment. Interest under the ETA is compounded daily at the prescribed annual rate on any reassessed tax.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with compliance administration distributed across the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential oversight, FINTRAC for AML/ATF and large cross-border EFT reporting, and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for currency/negotiable-instrument declaration at the border. Canada does not operate a restrictive foreign-exchange administration or central-bank FX licensing regime for ordinary trade and investment flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a fully freely convertible currency under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. Both current-account transactions (trade, services, royalties) and capital-account transactions (equity injection, shareholder loans, dividends, liquidation proceeds) are unrestricted and require no central-bank approval for conversion or repatriation. Profit remittance hurdles are tax-driven rather than FX-driven: 25% statutory Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents (treaty-reduced, e.g., 5%–15% under the Canada-United States treaty), 15%–25% on certain interest and royalties, the anti-surplus-stripping provisions of ITA sections 84.1 and 212.1, and paid-up-capital (PUC) verification. No blocking or foreign-exchange licensing exists; conversion is available at commercial bank rates through the free interbank market.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no surrender rules, no statutory surrender timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in any convertible currency in domestic or foreign-based accounts. The statutory obligations are reporting and record-keeping: cross-border electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported by financial institutions to FINTRAC; incoming/outgoing remittances substantiating capital contribution or trade settlement must be supported by the share-subscription ledger, commercial invoices, bills of lading/air waybills, and customs declarations (B3 form) for GST/HST zero-rating and statistical reporting. Border declaration of currency and monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more is mandatory for travellers under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account plus dedicated Capital Escrow Account for share-subscription funds and lease security holdback
Operational Account with USD operating sub-account and merchant settlement treasury pack
Operational Account with FX forward line and trade-finance documentary collection/LC services
Operational Account with Asia-Pacific trade desk (China/Hong Kong/Taiwan tea-origin corridor)
Operational Account with wholesale banking and US-dollar correspondent clearing
Operational Account alternative; regional treasury capability usable for back-up liquidity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.alberta_regional_alternative: ATB Financial (Alberta Treasury Branches) is the Alberta provincial Crown financial institution; it offers strong local relationship banking and business deposit accounts, but is not a Schedule I bank and has a narrower correspondent/FX hedging platform. Recommended only as a secondary operational account if the primary telex-based trade-finance relationship is held with a major Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as an auxiliary cross-border payment and low-value supplier settlement channel; LOW as a primary operational treasury account in Canada. Offshore digital EMI licences (e.g., UK FCA EMI or EU e-money institution) do not confer any Canadian banking or deposit-taking status. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), payment service providers operating for Canadians must be registered with the Bank of Canada; fund-holding activities are not CDIC-insured and generally expose the corporate to concentration risk. Wise (TransferWise) and Revolut Business may be used to pre-fund and pay tea/ceramics suppliers in CNY, HKD, JPY, or TWD, but Canadian-dollar settlement must run through the licensed Schedule I bank account to preserve treasury visibility and AML-compliant controls.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no Canadian statutory mandate requiring directors to appear physically in branch. In practice, Schedule I banks require either a physical in-branch appointment for at least one Canadian-resident signing officer (with government-issued gender-complete ID) or an equivalently robust interactive video verification where the applicant has a Canadian tax nexus and an existing Canadian banking relationship. Non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) will normally be subject to enhanced due diligence: certified true copies of passport, notarized proof of residential address, a banker's reference, and a video interview with a compliance officer. Remote opening without any physical step is generally impossible when the board is entirely non-resident; the recommended operating posture is to maintain a Canadian resident signatory (officer or local manager) to keep onboarding viability 'High'.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership held by non-resident individuals or non-resident entities with no Canadian tax footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated Alberta Corporate Registry extract showing the Corporate Access Number (CAN); register of individuals with significant control (ISC); notarized passport and address verification for each UBO; source-of-wealth statement; bank reference from the originating jurisdiction; Canadian tax identifier or T2/T1 proof for any Canadian nexus; organizational chart and trust deed if a trust is used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive specialty tea salon revenue model (POS sales and event cash) flagged as unexplained turnover
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: POS terminal merchant agreements; daily Z-read and X-read sales reports; inventory purchase invoices with tireless count reconciliation; commercial lease agreement proving physical lounge premises; credit-card settlement statements; GST/HST (QST where applicable) filings; CPA-reviewed cash-flow projections for the first four operating quarters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection sourced from high-risk jurisdiction, crypto off-ramp, or third-party person not identified on share registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the originating funding account; executed share subscription agreement and directors' resolution approving issuance; crypto exchange audit trail and wallet transaction history where crypto liquidation is concerned; gift deed or shareholder loan agreement with arm's-length interest rate; statutory declaration of source of funds; confirmation memo from a Canadian licensed CPA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid corporate history: shell formation, name change, or multiple beneficial-ownership transfers before bank onboarding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete Alberta Corporate Registry certificate of incorporation, restated articles and by-laws; chronological register of directors and shareholders since inception; explanation letter from counsel addressing each governance change; minutes of shareholders'/directors' meetings approving capital flows; confirmation of good standing from the Alberta service provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border disbursements to tea or ceramics suppliers with mismatches between invoices and customs declarations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices and purchase orders matched to supplier master file; export/import customs declarations (B3 and Canadian Customs Coding System); bills of lading/air waybills; supplier vetting documentation; goods description and HS codes (e.g., 0902 tea, 6914/6912 ceramics); logistics provider statements; annual compliance certificate from a customs broker.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital injections: use SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COV for cover settlement) to the Canadian beneficiary bank's SWIFT BIC (e.g., ROYCCAT2 for RBC, TDOMCATTTOR for TD), quoting the corporate's account number, the corporate legal name and the payment reference 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION CAPITAL - ALBERTA CORPORATE ACCOUNT - [ENTITY NAME]'. For CAD wires from the United States, utilize the Canadian bank's U.S. correspondent account (ABA) with Fedwire/CHIPS, followed by settlement over Canada's high-value Lynx system; for USD wires, instruct settlement into the USD operating sub-account. Preserve the share-subscription agreement, directors' resolution, share register, and receipts for each injection. FINTRAC EFT transaction reports are triggered at CAD 10,000 and above; all inbound injections must be reconcilable to the corporate's paid-up capital and disclosed on the annual return. For shareholder loans, use purpose reference 'INTERCOMPANY LOAN', execute a signed loan agreement, and apply the prescribed/proscribed interest rules under ITA section 15(2) and 17(1).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct wire transfers are the default rail for tea-leaf, ceramic-ware and packaging supplier payments — each MT103 must include supplier account details, invoice/PO numbers, and product description; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) are recommended for large seasonal procurement, typically sight or 30/60-day usance LCs issued by the Canadian bank in favour of the supplier's bank (especially in China, Japan, Taiwan and India); (3) Documentary collections (URC 522) on D/P or D/A terms are acceptable for mid-tier suppliers with established trade history; (4) Payments in USD, CNY, HKD or JPY should be pre-matched to FX forwards or swaps to lock margin; (5) SWIFT GPI tracking must be used for every cross-border disbursement; (6) all disbursements must be supported by commercial invoices, customs entry documentation, and supplier vetting records to satisfy the financial institution's ongoing transaction-monitoring obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright vanilla CAD/USD (and CAD/CNH where offered) FX forwards with tenors up to 12 months, executable under the bank's SME hedging facility, used to lock tea/ceramic import costs and export proceeds.
Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) converting USD-denominated import financing or supplier credit into CAD cash-flow exposure, used only where matched to a term loan or binding supply contract.

Vanilla European-style CAD/USD FX options (puts and calls) purchased from a licensed Canadian bank dealer to protect against adverse Canadian-dollar appreciation or depreciation on contingent seasonal purchase volumes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.fx_hedging_governance_notes: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not appropriate and are generally not offered internally for CAD because the Canadian dollar is deeply liquid and deliverable; all hedge transactions must evidence an underlying commercial exposure, be approved by the board in a formal treasury policy, and be executed under an ISDA or bank master FX agreement. No speculative hedging positions are permitted for a specialty tea salon wholesale/retail treasury.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or extra-provincial registration; e.g., an anniversary of May 15 requires filing by July 14.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD $100 applies after the 60-day window; failure to file for three consecutive years authorizes the Registrar to administratively dissolve the corporation without court order, and former directors may become jointly and severally liable for corporate debts under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the taxation year-end; a December 31 fiscal year-end requires filing no later than June 30 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month, up to 12 months (maximum 17%); continued non-filing may lead to CRA enforcement actions including criminal prosecution for gross negligence or wilful default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit applies only to a 'reporting issuer' under Alberta securities law. For a non-reporting private Alberta business corporation, an auditor is not required unless shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued voting shares submit a requisition or the directors voluntarily appoint one; lenders or existing credit covenants may impose an audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public and reporting-issuer entities must apply IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I); private enterprises may adopt either IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under Part II. CRA T2 filing schedules follow the chosen accounting framework but add prescribed corporate tax adjustments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not require a separate annual UBO filing to the Corporate Registry for an ordinary private corporation. The corporation must maintain an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) Register at its registered office and record any share transfer or change in significant control within 15 days. The annual return confirms directors and registered office information only and does not ask for shareholding data.
